extracted.intended_audience: researchers and practitioners studying peer review quality, editors, and NLP/ML researchers developing models and datasets for automated assessment of peer reviews
extracted.subtask_description: Creating and evaluating a dataset and models to classify scientific peer reviews as exhaustive vs. trivial, using sectional/aspect annotations and chain-of-thought prompting to align LLM judgements with human evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the review provides detailed, constructive feedback on the novelty of the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentioned in the abstract as one of the key aspects reviews should address (alongside clarity and theoretical soundness). No numeric scoring given on-page; treated as an aspect to be covered by exhaustive reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the review evaluates and comments on the clarity of the manuscript (explanations, presentation, readability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed in the abstract among aspects that detailed constructive reviews should cover. Implied that exhaustive reviews address clarity in detail across sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theoretical soundness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the review examines the theoretical foundations and soundness of claims and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named in the abstract as a central aspect for constructive feedback; exhaustive reviews are expected to evaluate theoretical soundness rather than merely state opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem statement (section coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the review inspects and comments on the paper's problem statement (motivation, scope, formulation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract lists 'problem statement' as a specific section that exhaustive reviews should cover; dataset/schema includes sectional annotations to capture this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Datasets (section coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the review inspects and comments on datasets used (appropriateness, quality, suitability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included in list of sections (problem statement, datasets, methodology, results) that exhaustive reviews should address; used as part of sectional annotations in labeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology (section coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the review analyzes the methods, experimental design, implementation details, and rigor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly identified as a key section exhaustive reviews should cover; part of sectional/aspect annotation schema in the dataset.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results (section coverage)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the review critiques results and their interpretation, statistical validity, and reported evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Named as a section to be covered by exhaustive reviews; reviewers/human annotators mark whether reviews address results as part of the labeling schema.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhaustiveness / Detailed analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: The review provides detailed analysis and covers key sections and critical aspects of a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors define exhaustive reviews as those 'providing detailed analysis and covering key sections and critical aspects of a paper' and argue these offer deeper insights that aid evaluation. The dataset labels reviews based on this property; illustrative CoT examples (Appendix A) show stepwise rationale for identifying exhaustiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionability of feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback includes actionable suggestions that authors can use to improve the manuscript (specific, prescriptive, or fixable recommendations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset classification explicitly uses 'actionable feedback' as a signal distinguishing exhaustive from trivial reviews. The abstract says classification is 'based on their thoroughness and actionable feedback.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Thoroughness
rubrics_metrics.description: The review is thorough in scope and depth (not cursory), examining multiple aspects and providing substantiated points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dataset is designed to separate reviews by 'thoroughness'; Appendix B and the abstract discuss human sectional/aspect annotations that operationalize thoroughness across review content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coverage of key sections and critical aspects
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the review mentions and evaluates the manuscript's major sections and critical conceptual/technical points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repeated theme in the paper: exhaustive reviews cover sections like problem statement, datasets, methodology, and results and address critical aspects; sectional annotations capture this coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to editorial decision-making (impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the review's depth and content are relevant and useful for editors in making acceptance/rejection decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract frames the dataset's purpose as helping editors 'evaluate each review’s impact on decision-making' by distinguishing exhaustive vs trivial reviews; relevance is treated as a downstream utility of exhaustiveness/actionability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional annotations (human labeling dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotate reviews by which manuscript sections they discuss (e.g., problem statement, datasets, methodology, results).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix B and the abstract note that human reviewers provide sectional annotations; these annotations form part of the dataset schema and labeling process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aspect annotations (human labeling dimension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Annotate reviews by specific aspects (novelty, clarity, theoretical soundness, actionability, etc.) addressed in the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper refers to 'sectional and aspect annotations by human reviewers'—aspect annotations operationalize the quality signals used to label exhaustive vs trivial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretability of model rationales
rubrics_metrics.description: How interpretable the model's internal reasoning or generated justification (e.g., CoT) is to humans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix B states Chain-of-Thought prompting outperformed other methods in interpretability; interpretability is used as an evaluation axis for prompting strategies when modeling reviewer justification and depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification accuracy (model performance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy (and other standard metrics) of models in classifying reviews as exhaustive vs trivial compared to human labels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paper uses quantitative analyses to measure classification accuracy of different LLM prompting strategies; CoT was reported to outperform Zero-/Few-Shot approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fairness and effectiveness of LLM variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether different LLMs perform fairly and effectively across review-classification tasks (including biases, consistency across review types).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract says both qualitative and quantitative analyses gauge 'fairness and effectiveness' of LLM variants; this is treated as an evaluative dimension when deploying automated assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trivial reviews (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews that are superficial, brief, lack substantive coverage of sections/aspects, and provide little or no actionable guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract contrasts trivial reviews with exhaustive ones: trivial reviews are 'more superficial' and do not provide the depth/actionable feedback that helps editors and authors; dataset labels such reviews accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain-of-Thought prompting efficacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of structured, stepwise Chain-of-Thought prompting to elicit model rationales that align with human judgements about review quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix B: CoT prompting achieved better interpretability and classification accuracy and produced more structured rationales compared to Zero-/Few-Shot prompting; authors provide CoT simulation and illustrative examples (Appendix A, Figures 4–5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical / integrity considerations regarding LLM use in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Potential risks when reviewers increasingly rely on LLMs, which may compromise the integrity of the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract highlights risks from reviewer reliance on LLMs and frames the dataset as a tool to study/model such effects; fairness/effectiveness analyses are recommended to detect harms.
